grammar.en: You can notice patterns. You learn vocabulary, and you can recognize the grammar instinctively.
grammar.zh: 你可以注意到规律。你学会了词汇，并且能够本能地识别语法。

grammar.en: Children seem to be better at learning things like pronunciation and those grammar aspects.
grammar.zh: 孩子们似乎更擅长学习发音和那些语法方面的东西。

grammar.en: Apply language immediately. Don’t wait until you feel ready to use new words or grammar.
grammar.zh: 立即应用语言。不要等到你觉得自己准备好了才去使用新单词或新语法。

grammar.en: You can't articulate the rules of grammar, yet you exercise them effortlessly when you speak.
grammar.zh: 你无法表述语法规则，但在说话时却能轻而易举地运用它们。

grammar.en: And as with all the grammar episodes, I’ll leave you with a final question.
grammar.zh: 和所有语法节目一样，我留给你一个最后的问题。

grind.en: But the men and women of the Andover workhouse went back to grinding bones.
grind.zh: 但安多弗济贫院的男男女女又回去研磨骨头了。

grind.en: Well, we already know that petrichor is the smell of the ground after rain.
grind.zh: 我们已经知道 petrichor 指的是雨后泥土的气味。

grind.en: They stood their ground, buoyed by the sense that this time, something was different.
grind.zh: 他们坚守阵地，受到了一种这次有所不同的感觉的鼓舞。

grind.en: Causeways are raised roads or paths built across water, wet ground, or low land.
grind.zh: 堤道是指建在水面、湿地或低洼地带上的高架道路或小径。

grind.en: So, the ground is shaking, music is blasting, and thousands of fans are dancing.
grind.zh: 所以，地面在震动，音乐在轰鸣，成千上万的粉丝在跳舞。

greenhouse.en: The main factor in climate change, of course, is human activity, especially greenhouse gas emissions.
greenhouse.zh: 当然，气候变化的主要因素是人类活动，尤其是温室气体排放。

greenhouse.en: Scientists have found that TRAPPIST-1e is not full of those greenhouse gases, they’ve ruled it out.
greenhouse.zh: 科学家发现 TRAPPIST-1e 并没有充满这些温室气体，他们已经排除了这种可能。

greenhouse.en: They both cool the planet by blocking sunlight, and they warm the planet because they have their own greenhouse effect.
greenhouse.zh: 它们既通过阻挡阳光来冷却地球，又因为它们自身的温室效应而使地球变暖。

greenhouse.en: Carbon emissions from food production make up around a third of all greenhouse gases, from the diesel used to drive tractors, to fertilisers, to cows and sheep producing methane.
greenhouse.zh: 粮食生产产生的碳排放约占所有温室气体的三分之一，从驱动拖拉机的柴油、化肥，到产生甲烷的牛羊。

greenhouse.en: Scientists have been looking at the potential atmosphere around TRAPPIST-1e and they've ruled out that it's really full of hydrogen or carbon dioxide, which is a great thing because they're greenhouse gases, which would make the planet really hot.
greenhouse.zh: 科学家们一直在研究 TRAPPIST-1e 周围的潜在大气层，他们已经排除了它充满氢气或二氧化碳的可能性，这太棒了，因为它们是温室气体，会让行星变得非常热。

growth.en: Another major success is economic growth and development, especially in newer members like Poland.
growth.zh: 另一个重大的成功是经济增长和发展，特别是在像波兰这样较新的成员国中。

growth.en: So all of this growth and excitement creates a lot of attention and investment.
growth.zh: 因此，所有这些增长和狂热吸引了大量的关注和投资。

growth.en: ‘Cause feedback is really important. A growth mindset involves being willing to change, right?
growth.zh: 因为反馈真的很重要。成长型思维包含着愿意改变的意愿，对吧？

growth.en: And there are now many debates over immigration, identity, climate change, and economic growth.​
growth.zh: 如今围绕移民、身份认同、气候变化和经济增长也存在着许多辩论。​

growth.en: Under Ottoman Rule, the city of Istanbul experienced a long period of growth and peace.
growth.zh: 在奥斯曼帝国的统治下，伊斯坦布尔经历了一个漫长的增长和平静时期。

greeting.en: Here, presenter Claudia Hammond and guest Pete Olusoga discuss what listeners had to say: Rachel in Manchester says what annoys her is people who start their emails with just your name and without a simple greeting like 'hi'.
greeting.zh: 在这里，主持人克劳迪娅·哈蒙德和嘉宾皮特·奥卢索加讨论了听众的看法：来自曼彻斯特的瑞秋说，最让她恼火的是那些发邮件时只写你的名字，连一声像“嗨”这样简单的问候都没有的人。

grasp.en: It's called Stroke. You're awake And trying to grasp who it is.
grasp.zh: 它叫《中风》。你醒着，试图弄清楚这是谁。

grasp.en: It wouldn't even be easy wins. It would be the, the toil and the struggle of achieving and reaching for things that are right out of grasp that are right above my threshold and continuing to do that, to like lift the weight, to build the muscle, to break it down and do it over and over again, because like, that's what creates the character traits that are the man that I want to be.
grasp.zh: 甚至连简单的胜利都不会有。那将是辛勤的耕耘和挣扎，去追求那些触手可及却又刚好超出我阈值的东西，并持续这样做，就像举重一样，为了练就肌肉，不断地破坏它、重建它，一遍又一遍，因为这正是塑造我想要成为的那种人的性格特质。

grasp.en: But, the idea that Smith saw self-interest--which I think we think of usually as grasping, or as how I come down when I'm faced with a choice, say in a negotiation whether to leave money on the table or not, should I put myself first, and so on--there's such a broader view of that self-interest that you capture that is about our desire to remake the world in our own image, to forge it, to craft it, and your view that that's really what growth is about.
grasp.zh: 但斯密所理解的自利——我们通常把自利理解为贪婪，或者理解为我在面临选择时会怎么做，比如在谈判中要不要把利益留一部分在桌面上，要不要把自己放在第一位，诸如此类——你所捕捉到的这种自利，其实有一个宽广得多的视角，它关乎我们想要按照自己的模样去重塑世界、去锻造它、去打磨它的欲望，而你的看法是，这才是经济增长真正的意义所在。

grassy.en: Against a grassy background, they stand out easily.
grassy.zh: 在草地背景的衬托下，它们很容易脱颖而出。

grey.en: Their clothes would be taken away, to be replaced by a rough grey uniform.
grey.zh: 他们的衣服会被收走，换上粗糙的灰色制服。

grey.en: Ground to a fine powder, it is, says Mathilde, grey dust.
grey.zh: Mathilde 说，把它磨成细粉，就是灰色的尘土。”

grey.en: The man in the grey coat spoke calmly and authoritatively.
grey.zh: 那位身穿灰色外套的男子说话时语气平静、颇具权威感。

grey.en: Grey pepper is an industrial creation, not a botanical one.
grey.zh: 灰胡椒是一种工业产物，而不是植物学上的产物。

grey.en: I’m Phil. And I’m Beth. Grey hairs, wrinkles, and poor eyesight are common signs that our body is growing old.
grey.zh: 我是Phil。我是Beth。白发、皱纹和视力下降是我们身体变老的常见迹象。

graduate.en: And also employers are much more cautious about sponsoring overseas graduates because it’s expensive.
graduate.zh: 而且雇主在赞助海外毕业生时也更加谨慎，因为这很昂贵。

graduate.en: This is the visa a student is eligible for after they graduate from university.
graduate.zh: 这是学生从大学毕业后有资格获得的签证。

graduate.en: But after graduating, he found real life to be not quite as easy.
graduate.zh: 但毕业后，他发现现实生活并没有那么容易。

graduate.en: He graduated in 2009 with the highest honours, with a degree in political science and philosophy.
graduate.zh: 他在2009年以最高荣誉毕业，获得了政治学和哲学学位。

graduate.en: There was the graduated escalation that made each individual step seem small.
graduate.zh: 还有那种循序渐进的升级方式，让每一小步看起来都微不足道。

graceful.en: The swimmer's movements need to be as graceful as a ballet dancer, and above all, it has to look effortless because judges award points for artistic expression.
graceful.zh: 游泳运动员的动作需要像芭蕾舞演员一样优雅，而且最重要的是，它必须看起来毫不费力，因为裁判会根据艺术表现力来打分。

gray.en: First, let's meet Roushanna Gray, a wild-food forager living in Cape Point, South Africa.
gray.zh: 首先，让我们认识一下居住在南非开普角的野食采集者 Roushanna Gray。

gray.en: Let's listen as British food historian Annie Gray and Argentinian chef Barbara Oievari tell BBC World Service programme The Food Chain what they like to snack on between meals: I like salted peanuts and I love a banana – preferably together, actually.
gray.zh: 让我们听听英国饮食史学家 Annie Gray 和阿根廷厨师 Barbara Oievari 在 BBC World Service 节目 The Food Chain 中讲述他们两餐之间喜欢吃什么零食：我喜欢咸花生，我也很喜欢香蕉——其实最好能一起吃。

gray.en: This meal that you're having, just taste these ingredients what what is taste feel it on your on your on your taste buds and and like one of the tools they they teach you like with adhd sometimes you know when when it when it makes you go into anxiety or depression is to just notice things practice being present walk down the street and like look like really look and say out loud what you're seeing and at first it's very stupid that is a red door that is a green roof that is a pigeon sitting on the gutter that is a gutter, that is a gray car that is driven by.
gray.zh: 你正在吃的这顿饭，只是品尝这些成分，什么……什么是味道，在你的味蕾上感受它，然后……他们教你的工具之一，有时你知道，当ADHD让你陷入焦虑或抑郁时，就是去注意事物。练习活在当下。走在街上，像……真正地看，并大声说出你所看到的。起初这很愚蠢：那是一扇红色的门，那是一个绿色的屋顶，那是一只鸽子坐在排水沟上，那是一个排水沟，那是一辆灰色的车，由……驾驶。

gray.en: But as long as you're learning and you keep iterating fast and cutting your losses quickly, then when you find the right thing, you have to be optimistic and compound into it. so you don't want to jump into the first thing you don't want to marry the first person you date necessarily unless you got very lucky but you you want to investigate and explore very very quickly until you find the match and then you have to be willing to go all in you have to be willing to move your chips at the center of the table so both those uh both those uh approaches are required so it's a barbell strategy it's sort of black or it's white and most people are sort of stuck in this gray bit and like half in but i'm kind of don't really know if i am and i also think like labels like pessimists optimists cynic introvert extrovert these are very self-limiting humans are very dynamic there are times when you feel like being introverted there are times when you feel like being extroverted there are contexts in which you'll be pessimistic there are contexts in which you'll be optimistic leave all the labels alone It's better just to look at the problem at hand, look at reality the way it is.
gray.zh: 但只要你在学习，并且保持快速迭代和快速止损，那么当你找到正确的事情时，你必须保持乐观并投入其中。所以你不想跳进第一件事，你不一定非要嫁给第一个约会的人，除非你非常幸运，但你想非常非常快地调查和探索，直到找到匹配的对象，然后你必须愿意全力以赴，你必须愿意把筹码推到桌子中央。所以这两种方法都是必需的，这是一种杠铃策略，它是黑的或者是白的，而大多数人被困在这个灰色的地带，半推半就，但我不太确定我是否是这样。我也认为像悲观主义者、乐观主义者、愤世嫉俗者、内向者、外向者这样的标签是非常自我限制的。人类是非常动态的，有时你会觉得想内向，有时你会觉得想外向，在某些情况下你会悲观，在某些情况下你会乐观。把所有的标签都抛开吧，最好只是看看手头的问题，看看现实本来的样子。

graph.en: But have you seen these graphs before? Have you seen those graphs before?
graph.zh: 但你以前见过这些图表吗？你以前见过那些图表吗？

graph.en: But have you seen these graphs before? Have you seen those graphs before?
graph.zh: 但你以前见过这些图表吗？你以前见过那些图表吗？

graph.en: It’s a graph that shows levels of ability and confidence.
graph.zh: 这是一张展示能力水平与自信水平的图表。

graph.en: Her hit song, Cruel Summer, created a peak - the highest point - in the graph which James's machine was drawing.
graph.zh: 她的热门歌曲《Cruel Summer》在James的机器正在绘制的图表中创造了一个峰值——最高点。

graph.en: In this top graph of the red wiggly line, we're looking at the ground velocity in essentially metres per second.
graph.zh: 在这个红色波浪线的顶部图表中，我们本质上是在观察每秒米数的地面速度。

gradual.en: Some people wanted gradual reform. Others demanded independence right now.
gradual.zh: 有些人想要渐进式改革。另一些人则要求立刻独立。

gradual.en: If you do something slowly but surely, you do it in a gradual but reliable way which will achieve the result you want.
gradual.zh: 如果你稳扎稳打地做某事，你就会用一种循序渐进但可靠的方式来达到你想要的结果。

gradual.en: When it comes to decluttering your home, it's best to do things slowly but surely – in a gradual but reliable way which will achieve the result you want.
gradual.zh: 当谈到清理家里的杂物时，最好稳扎稳打——用一种循序渐进但可靠的方式来达到你想要的结果。

gradual.en: This is very dangerous for democracy. Bernardo thinks Portugal has seen an erosion of trust – a term for the gradual weakening of people's confidence in political and economic institutions, and the government in office.
gradual.zh: 这对于民主来说非常危险。Bernardo认为葡萄牙的信任度正在流失——这是一个用来形容人们对政治经济机构以及现任政府的信心逐渐减弱的术语。

gradually.en: It no longer needed to rely on Britain. Full legal independence, however, came gradually.
gradually.zh: 它不再需要依赖英国。然而，完全的法律独立是一个渐进的过程。

gradually.en: An erosion of trust happens when people gradually lose confidence in political and economic institutions.
gradually.zh: 当人们对政治和经济机构的信心逐渐丧失时，就会发生信任流失（erosion of trust）。

gradually.en: Gradually he noticed things that changed the way he understood nature and life.
gradually.zh: 渐渐地，他注意到了一些事情，这些事情改变了他对自然和生命的理解。

gradually.en: Lyell’s work argued that the earth had changed gradually over incredibly long periods of time.
gradually.zh: Lyell的著作论证了地球在极其漫长的时间里发生了渐进式的改变。

gradually.en: Throughout the 20th century, the Vice Presidency gradually morphed into a position with real influence.
gradually.zh: 在整个20世纪，副总统职位逐渐演变成一个具有真正影响力的职位。

grace.en: For five months during the Covid pandemic, Australian engineer Grace Brown had no human contact.
grace.zh: 在新冠疫情期间的五个月里，澳大利亚工程师格蕾丝·布朗没有任何人类接触。

grace.en: My mom's definitely remarkable. But as she would say, it's by the grace of God.
grace.zh: 我妈妈确实很了不起。但正如她所说，那是上帝的恩典。

grace.en: But it ended up kind of being my saving grace in my recovery.
grace.zh: 但它最终成为了我康复过程中的救命稻草。

grace.en: I'm like, you know what? Maybe give her a little grace, you know?
grace.zh: 我在想，你知道吗？也许对她多一点宽容吧，你知道吗？

grace.en: I loved the show Will and Grace, but I'm like, I cannot watch this show because Satan is watching me.
grace.zh: 我很喜欢《威尔和格蕾丝》这部剧，但我想：我不能看这个剧，因为撒旦在看着我呢。

gratitude.en: To take something for granted means to not appreciate or show gratitude for something which helps you.
gratitude.zh: 把某事视为理所当然（to take something for granted）意味着不感激或不感谢那些帮助过你的事情。

gratitude.en: I think all you can do is kind of cultivate an appreciation and gratitude for what you have.
gratitude.zh: 我认为你所能做的就是培养对你所拥有的东西的欣赏和感激。

gratitude.en: There are simple things anyone can do, starting with gratitude – feeling thankful and appreciative for what you have.
gratitude.zh: 任何人都可以做一些简单的事情，从感恩开始——对你所拥有的感到感激和欣赏。

gratitude.en: So, things that are as simple as just practising gratitude, right?
gratitude.zh: 所以，事情其实很简单，比如练习感恩，对吧？

gratitude.en: And from a gratitude perspective, my most powerful frame for gratitude has been thinking about my 85 year old self, waking up as my 30 year old self.
gratitude.zh: 从感恩的角度来看，我最强大的感恩框架是想象我85岁时的自己，醒来时变成了30岁的我。

grant.en: If you take something for granted, you accept or assume it without question.
grant.zh: 如果你把某事视为理所当然，你就会毫无疑问地接受或假设它。

grant.en: If you take something for granted, you fail to value or appreciate something which benefits you.
grant.zh: 如果你把某事视为理所当然，你就会忽视或不感激对你有益的事情。

grant.en: And in 2013, he was granted a royal pardon, formally overturning his conviction.
grant.zh: 2013 年，他获得了皇家特赦，正式推翻了对他的定罪。

grant.en: To take something for granted means to not appreciate or show gratitude for something which helps you.
grant.zh: 把某事视为理所当然（to take something for granted）意味着不感激或不感谢那些帮助过你的事情。

grant.en: But I think we should never take for granted how many times that doesn't happen.
grant.zh: 但我认为我们永远不应该认为这是理所当然的，因为很多时候这种情况并没有发生。

grasshopper.en: I'm Georgie. And I'm Beth. Georgie, what do apples, carrots and celery have in common with insects like beetles, crickets and grasshoppers?
grasshopper.zh: 我是乔治。我是贝丝。乔治，苹果、胡萝卜和西红柿有什么共同点，跟甲虫、蟋蟀和蚂蚱这些昆虫一样？

graze.en: Doc Holliday was grazed. Wyatt walked away without injury.
graze.zh: Doc Holliday 只是被擦伤，Wyatt 则毫发无损地走了出来。

graze.en: In English, you can also say a person is grazing if they continually eat snacks or little bites of food.
graze.zh: 在英语里，如果一个人不停地吃零食或一小口一小口地吃东西，也可以说他在 grazing。

graze.en: G razers are animals, like cows, which do this, and a person who grazes continually eats little bites of food.
graze.zh: grazers 指的是像牛这样以此为食的动物，而一个 grazes(不停小口进食)的人，则是指不停吃零食的人。

grab.en: Known as clickbait, headlines like these are used to grab your attention and make you read more.
grab.zh: 这类被称为“标题党”的标题，目的就是吸引你的眼球，让你阅读更多内容。

grab.en: Then people starting grabbing their computers and their copy machines and rolling them out of the building.
grab.zh: 然后人们开始抢搬他们的电脑和复印机，把它们滚出大楼。

grab.en: So Brandy stopped at a store, ran in and grabbed the diapers.
grab.zh: 于是 Brandy 在一家商店停了下来，跑进去拿了尿布。

grab.en: You know, and I do think in life, you have to let go of something old to grab onto something new.
grab.zh: 你知道，我确实认为在生活中，你必须放下旧的东西才能抓住新的东西。

grab.en: She grabbed the card and ran out the door.

grip.en: So you grip tightly. That's right. The worst outcome in the world is not having self-esteem.
grip.zh: 所以你抓得很紧。没错。世上最糟糕的结果就是没有自尊。

grip.en: Mobutu’s grip on power wasn’t just psychological; it was brutally enforced.
grip.zh: 蒙博托对权力的掌控不仅仅停留在心理层面，而是靠残酷的手段强力推行。

grip.en: If an idea takes grip on something, it takes control of it.
grip.zh: 如果一个观点“takes grip”（扎根），它就占据了主导地位。

grip.en: When you say an idea has taken grip on something, you mean it's taken control of it.
grip.zh: 当你对某种观点说它“taken grip”（扎根/占主导地位）时，意思就是它已经占据了控制地位。

grip.en: It certainly seems that he had lost all grip on reality.
grip.zh: 看起来他确实已经完全脱离了现实。

grunt.en: At 75 volts, the learner grunted. At 120 volts, he called out that the shocks were becoming painful.
grunt.zh: 电压到75伏特时，“学生”发出了痛哼声。到120伏特时，他大声喊出电击开始让他感到疼痛。

grim.en: The grim irony here is that Willis was considered a relatively enlightened practitioner.
grim.zh: 这里残酷的讽刺在于，Willis 被认为是一位相对开明的从业者。

grim.en: Young people, who made up a huge chunk of Egypt’s 100 million-strong population, faced a grim future.
grim.zh: 年轻人占了埃及 1 亿人口的很大一部分，他们面对的是一个黯淡的未来。

grim.en: And life inside, well, it was incredibly grim.
grim.zh: 至于里面的生活，嗯，简直阴暗得难以置信。

grim.en: It was a grim lesson in how “civilised” nations could turn technology and organisation into instruments of mass destruction.
grim.zh: 这是一次残酷的教训，让他们看清了“文明”国家如何将技术和组织变成大规模毁灭的工具。

grim.en: It was seriously grim, and an estimated 10 million Congolese people were killed directly and indirectly in the first 23 years of Belgian colonisation alone.
grim.zh: 这极其残酷，据估计，仅在比利时殖民统治的前23年里，就有大约1000万刚果人直接或间接丧生。

grain.en: The treadmill had originally been used to pump water or grind grain.
grain.zh: 跑步机最初是用来抽水或磨谷物的。

grain.en: Ergot, to be exact. Ergot grows on rye, a grain the Puritans used to make bread.
grain.zh: 确切地说，是麦角菌。麦角菌生长在黑麦上，而黑麦正是清教徒用来做面包的谷物。

grain.en: These people did not rely on large scale agriculture of grains.
grain.zh: 这些人并不依赖大规模的谷物农业。

grain.en: This could contain vegetables and grains and, if times were good, maybe a little bit of meat or fish.
grain.zh: 这里面可能含有蔬菜和谷物，如果日子过得好，也许还会有一点点肉或鱼。

grain.en: Most societies had a grain, wheat or rice or maize, but in Peru, they did not have some kind of basic grain.
grain.zh: 大多数社会都有一种谷物，小麦、大米或玉米，但在秘鲁，他们没有某种基础谷物。

grateful.en: And there were many days. Again, I mean, I'm just so grateful and I'm so lucky.
grateful.zh: 而且有很多天。再说一次，我的意思是，我非常感激，我非常幸运。

grateful.en: You know, I've never, like I, every time I look at her, I'm grateful that she exists.
grateful.zh: 你知道，我从来没有，每次我看着她，我都感激她存在。

grateful.en: And I think like, I was very grateful. So one of my biggest inspirations or whatever, you know, influences when I was in Baltimore was I would have lunch with my grandfather three times a week.
grateful.zh: 而且我觉得，我很感激。我在巴尔的摩时，我最大的灵感来源之一，或者说对我影响很大的人，是我每周有三天会跟我爷爷一起吃午饭。

grateful.en: One witness testified that the inmates had been so hungry that when a horse died in the yard, they had been grateful, because it meant more bones to grind, and more scraps to fight over.
grateful.zh: 一位证人作证说，院民们饿得实在没办法，当院子里有一匹马死掉时，他们竟然心存感激，因为这意味着有更多的骨头可以磨，有更多的残渣可以争抢。

grateful.en: But she's very grateful for Miss Betsy and everything she's done, because she's somebody who, without even asking for anything in return, gave my mom a hand and has just been there to help us with whatever it is that we need every step of the way.
grateful.zh: 不过她真的很感激Betsy DeVos女士以及她所做的一切，因为她是不求任何回报、向我妈妈伸出援手的人，而且每一步都在我们需要的时候给予帮助。

greedy.en: He wasn't a nice man. He was cunning, lazy, greedy, and easily upset.
greedy.zh: 他不是个好人。他狡猾、懒惰、贪婪，而且很容易暴躁。

greedy.en: And they often feature an innocent homeowner who was duped by a lying, greedy mortgage banker.
greedy.zh: 而且它们通常的主角都是一个被说谎、贪婪的房贷银行家欺骗的无辜房主。

greedy.en: To some, this is a worthy achievement, a law that protects workers from exploitation at the hands of greedy corporations.
greedy.zh: 对某些人来说，这是一项了不起的成就，是一部保护工人免受贪婪公司剥削的法律。

greedy.en: Or if you're more of a Wall Street Journal editorial page type, an innocent mortgage banker who was duped by lying, greedy homeowner.
greedy.zh: 或者如果你更倾向于《华尔街日报》社论版的口味，那就是一个被说谎、贪婪的房主欺骗的无辜房贷银行家。

grand.en: Grand buildings and palaces, and public spaces were built, and they transformed the city’s appearance.
grand.zh: 宏伟的建筑、宫殿和公共空间拔地而起，改变了城市的风貌。

grand.en: The population grew. Wealthy nobles built grand palaces and elegant residences in Warsaw.
grand.zh: 人口增长了。富有的贵族们在华沙建造了宏伟的宫殿和优雅的宅邸。

grand.en: In just community conversations with people, we knew she hadn't been deeply involved in Grand Rapids Public.
grand.zh: 在与大家的日常交流中，我们知道她并没有深度参与过Grand Rapids Public。

grand.en: In French, they are called “grands nez”—which means “great nose.”
grand.zh: 在法语中，他们被称为“grands nez”——意思是“大鼻子”。

grand.en: I visited her during summer vacation at her house in Grand Rapids.
grand.zh: 暑假期间，我在她位于大急流城的家中拜访了她。

grandfather.en: His father died when he was only 8 years old, and his uncle and grandfather stepped up as sort of joint father figures.
grandfather.zh: 在他仅8岁时父亲就去世了，他的叔叔和外祖父充当了某种共同的父亲角色。

grandfather.en: So, George III was born in 1738. As the name suggests, he was the third king called George; the other two were his great-grandfather, George I, and his grandfather, George II.
grandfather.zh: 那么，George III 出生于 1738 年。顾名思义，他是第三个叫 George 的国王；另外两个是他的曾祖父 George I 和祖父 George II。

grandfather.en: And I think like, I was very grateful. So one of my biggest inspirations or whatever, you know, influences when I was in Baltimore was I would have lunch with my grandfather three times a week.
grandfather.zh: 而且我觉得，我很感激。我在巴尔的摩时，我最大的灵感来源之一，或者说对我影响很大的人，是我每周有三天会跟我爷爷一起吃午饭。

grandfather.en: I often think of everyone that I meet, but also myself through the context of like, I guess a similar analogy, like a set of ingredients that came together that were then put into an oven and like, the heat was turned on and we were bait not to say that we can't be changed after that moment but um what are those ingredients so my mother south african and hossa woman uh my father swiss from switzerland but was living in south africa so those are those are the parental ingredients you know my grandmother i think is a key ingredient because i spent a lot of time with her as a young child my grandfather was a crazy funny man was bipolar but we didn't know at the time i think we knew towards the end of his life but it made him wildly entertaining.
grandfather.zh: 我经常通过一种类比来审视我遇到的每一个人，也包括我自己，就像是一堆成分混合在一起，放进烤箱，加热，然后我们就出炉了——并不是说在那之后我们就不能改变了，但那些成分是什么呢？我母亲是南非科萨族女性，我父亲是瑞士人，但他当时住在南非，所以这些是父母给的成分。我觉得我祖母是一个关键成分，因为我小时候和她待在一起的时间很长。我祖父是个疯狂有趣的人，他患有躁郁症，但当时我们不知道，我想直到他生命末期我们才意识到，但这让他变得极其有娱乐性。

grants.en: Salaries are lower, there are fewer job opportunities, fewer opportunities for investment or grants for starting new businesses.
grants.zh: 薪资更低，工作机会更少，获得创业投资或补助金的机会也更少。

grants.en: We are no longer talking about diplomacy and land grants.
grants.zh: 我们谈论的不再是外交和土地授予。

grants.en: Under this policy, they would give up their traditional Gaelic titles, acknowledge Henry as king, and receive their lands back as English-style grants with titles like Earl or Baron.
grants.zh: 根据这项政策，他们将放弃传统的盖尔头衔，承认 Henry 为国王，并以伯爵或男爵等英国式头衔重新获得自己的土地。

grants.en: DOGE’s website proudly displayed a “Wall of Receipts,” listing thousands of terminated contracts and grants, with savings they claimed reached $205 billion by August 2025, a savings of $1,273.29 per taxpayer.
grants.zh: DOGE 的网站自豪地展示了一面“收据墙”，上面列出了数千份被终止的合同和赠款，并声称截至 2025 年 8 月节省的资金达到了 2050 亿美元，相当于为每个纳税人节省了 1,273.29 美元。

grandson.en: From father to eldest son. And if that son has died, then to the grandson.
grandson.zh: 从父亲传给长子。如果那个长子已经去世，则传给孙子。

grandson.en: He was the son of the heroic general Germanicus and the adopted grandson of Rome’s first emperor, Augustus.
grandson.zh: 他是英雄将军 Germanicus 的儿子，也是罗马第一位皇帝 Augustus 的养孙。

grandson.en: It has been ruled by the same family since 1948: first Kim Il-sung, then his son Kim Jong-il, and now his grandson Kim Jong-un.
grandson.zh: 自1948年以来，它一直由同一个家族统治：先是金日成(Kim Il-sung)，然后是他的儿子金正日，现在是他的孙子金正恩。

grandson.en: She was tough, fiercely loyal, deeply religious in her own way, and utterly determined that her grandson would not be swallowed up by the circumstances around him.
grandson.zh: 她性格刚强，极其忠诚，以她自己独特的方式笃信宗教，并且坚决不让自己的孙子被周围的环境吞没。

grandson.en: Instead of moving vertically — father → son → grandson — the throne could move horizontally, from brother to brother, staying within the founder’s generation for as long as possible.
grandson.zh: 王位不是垂直传递——父亲 → 儿子 → 孙子，而是可以在兄弟之间水平传递，尽可能长时间地保留在创立者那一代人手中。

grandmother.en: My grandmother would tell us stories of how, because she had the best memory in the family.
grandmother.zh: 我祖母会给我们讲故事，因为她是家里记忆力最好的人。

grandmother.en: So I spent most of my time with my mom, with my grandmother, with my grandmother and my grandmother's friends.
grandmother.zh: 所以我大部分时间都和我妈妈、我祖母、我祖母和她朋友们在一起。

grandmother.en: They spread to people no one expected: a 71-year-old grandmother who went to church every Sunday and a well-respected farmer.
grandmother.zh: 它们蔓延到了意想不到的人身上：一个每个星期天都去教堂的71岁祖母，以及一个备受尊敬的农夫。

grandmother.en: And by the time Vance was around fifteen or sixteen years old, he had moved out of his mother's home permanently and was living with his grandmother.
grandmother.zh: 到了 Vance 大约十五六岁的时候，他已经彻底搬出了母亲的家，和祖母住在一起。

grandmother.en: Then you take care of your extended family, you take care of your cousins, brothers, uncles, grandmothers, aunts, sisters, everybody that you can. and then if you have more resources beyond that then you go take care of your local tribe you take care of your people you start trying to do some good for the world and if you have more resources than that you go take care of an even bigger tribe and that's how you earn both respect and self-confidence and you live up to your potential so the the more you have the more is rightfully expected of you and i think it's a good compact with society when highly capable people express and flex that capability by giving more and more and by doing more and more and society rewards them with the one thing they can't get otherwise, which is status.
grandmother.zh: 然后你照顾你的大家庭，照顾你的堂表亲、兄弟、叔叔、祖母、阿姨、姐妹，所有你能照顾的人。如果在此之外你还有更多资源，那么你就去照顾你的当地部落，照顾你的人民，开始尝试为世界做点好事。如果你拥有的资源比那还多，你就去照顾一个更大的部落，这就是你赢得尊重和自信的方式，你才能发挥出你的潜力。所以你拥有的越多，人们理所当然对你的期望就越高。我认为当高能力的人通过给予更多、做更多来表达和展示这种能力时，这与社会达成了一种良好的契约，而社会则用他们无法通过其他方式获得的东西来奖励他们，那就是地位。

groan.en: His parents rushed to meet him, but as they approached the aeroplane, they heard this raw, almost animalistic groaning, like a primordial cry for help.
groan.zh: 他的父母赶去接他，但当他们靠近飞机时，听到的是一阵原始而近乎野兽般的呻吟声，像是一种最本能的求救呼喊。

greet.en: Any guest at one of his parties would be greeted with a flute of Pink Laurent Perrier champagne.
greet.zh: 任何参加他派对的客人都将受到一杯粉红罗兰百瑞香槟的迎接。

greet.en: He was only 30 years old. Now, when this sentence was announced, it was greeted with a mixture of horror and praise.
greet.zh: 当时他只有 30 岁。当这一判决公布时，人们的反应喜忧参半，既有震惊也有赞许。

greet.en: He is too old and weak to get up, and Odysseus knows that he cannot greet him, lest his identity be revealed.
greet.zh: 它太老弱了，已经站不起来了，奥德修斯也知道自己不能上前打招呼，以免暴露身份。

greet.en: And so when I was in the meet and greet line to meet him, he said to me, we already know each other.
greet.zh: 所以当我排队等着和他见面握手时，他对我说，我们已经认识了。

greet.en: As his secretary, he chose Mobutu. But if you are thinking of “secretary” as an administrative helper who brought coffee and tea, and greeted guests at the reception, no, Mobutu was a very different kind of secretary.
greet.zh: 他选择了蒙博托作为他的秘书。但如果你把“秘书”想象成一个端茶倒水、在接待处迎宾的行政助理，那就大错特错了，蒙博托是另一种完全不同的秘书。

grave.en: In 1914, German archaeologists found a grave that dates back 14,000 years, to a time when you might have thought dogs had a purely functional purpose.
grave.zh: 1914年，德国考古学家发现了一座可以追溯到1.4万年前的墓穴，那是一个你可能会觉得狗只有纯粹功能性用途的时代。

greatly.en: This, clearly, was not a very democratic system, so it was reformed, and the number of what’s called hereditary peers was greatly reduced.
greatly.zh: 很明显，这不是一个非常民主的体系，所以它进行了改革，被称为世袭贵族的数量大大减少。

greatly.en: Some parts of Nigeria have benefited greatly from oil production, some people as well, but most ordinary Nigerians haven’t seen as much improvement in their daily lives as you would expect.
greatly.zh: 尼日利亚的一些地区从石油生产中受益匪浅，一些人也是如此，但大多数普通尼日利亚人并没有看到他们的日常生活有你所期望的那么多改善。

greatly.en: Cassandra complex at global scale. And I would argue that large percentages of the population are essentially just infected with these mimetic viruses that have taken over their brain and are causing them to do incredible gyration about things that probably aren't even true or are greatly exaggerated.
greatly.zh: 全球规模的卡珊德拉情结。我认为很大一部分人口本质上就是被这些模因病毒感染了，这些病毒接管了他们的大脑，导致他们对那些可能根本不是事实，或者被严重夸大的事情做出惊人的反应。

grammatical.en: Every word, phrase, or grammatical structure I learned had a purpose.
grammatical.zh: 我学的每一个单词、短语或语法结构都有一个目的。

grammatical.en: They used a technique called forensic linguistics, which is the study of language in a legal context, and the experts noted identical usages of certain uncommon words and specific, idiosyncratic grammatical constructions.
grammatical.zh: 他们使用了一种叫做司法语言学（forensic linguistics）的技术，这是在法律背景下对语言的研究，专家们注意到某些不常见词汇的相同用法以及特定的、独特的语法结构。

gross.en: A wonderful researcher named James Gross, for example, at Stanford University, who is studying the way in which we manage our emotions, primarily through cognition, for decades and decades.
gross.zh: 比如斯坦福大学一位很出色的研究者詹姆斯·格罗斯，他几十年来一直在研究，我们主要是通过认知手段来管理自己情绪的方式。

gross.en: Fast forward to the modern era, and we have scientists, statisticians, economists and even governments trying to measure happiness, using it as a yardstick for the well-being of a country, as an alternative to metrics like GDP, Gross Domestic Product.
gross.zh: 快进到现代，我们有科学家、统计学家、经济学家甚至政府，他们试图用幸福来衡量一个国家的福祉，将其作为国内生产总值（GDP）等指标的替代方案。

grape.en: That's fundamental. It's sour grapes at an existential level, right?
grape.zh: 这很根本。这是一种存在主义层面的吃不到葡萄说葡萄酸，对吧？

grape.en: Nobody seemed to have told the young emperor anything; nobody had slipped over on a stray grape or spilled the wine over someone’s head.
grape.zh: 似乎没人给这位年轻的皇帝讲过什么事；没人踩在落单的葡萄上滑倒，也没人把酒洒在别人的头上。

grape.en: Yeah. Related to the sort of cynicism thing that we were talking about earlier, and I call it the cynicism safety blanket, that sour grapes at an existential level.
grape.zh: 是的。这与我们之前谈论的那种愤世嫉俗有关，我称之为“愤世嫉俗的安全毯”，那是存在主义层面的“酸葡萄”。

granddaughter.en: What’s more, he was married to a granddaughter of Augustus, Agrippina the Elder.
granddaughter.zh: 更重要的是，他娶了 Augustus 的孙女大 Agrippina。

grocery.en: So I wasn't going to the grocery store. My house wasn't unpacked yet.
grocery.zh: 所以我没有去杂货店。我的房子还没拆包。

grocery.en: It seemed like a lot to me. But I was living at home with my parents, I didn’t pay rent, and I didn’t pay for groceries.
grocery.zh: 对我来说，这似乎很多。但我当时和父母住在一起，不用付房租，也不用买菜。

grieve.en: It's a very strange experience to have because I grieved somebody.
grieve.zh: 这是一种非常奇怪的经历，因为我为某人悲伤。

grieve.en: I grieved the loss of my mother, but then she didn't die.
grieve.zh: 我为失去母亲而悲伤，但她没有死。

grieve.en: I’ll be honest with you, it was tough. I grieved; I mourned; and I had to start over, as a writer.
grieve.zh: 说实话，这很难。我感到悲伤；我感到哀悼；我不得不作为一名作家重新开始。

grieve.en: The winter was brutal, crops had failed, smallpox had swept through, and Indian raids from the north had left families grieving.
grieve.zh: 冬天残酷无情，庄稼绝收，天花肆虐，北方的印第安人袭击更是让许多家庭陷入失去亲人的悲痛之中。

gramme.en: Dogs, cats and rats were killed to supplement the miserable 125 grammes of bread a day that each resident was allocated.
gramme.zh: 狗、猫和老鼠都被杀来吃，以勉强维持每人每天仅有125克面包的可怜配给。

gravity.en: There is no gravity on an asteroid, so everything would need to be tied down to the asteroid.
gravity.zh: 小行星上没有引力，所以所有的东西都必须绑在小行星上。

gravity.en: And Isaac Newton in one year changed the way that we understand physics and forces and gravity.
gravity.zh: 艾萨克·牛顿在短短一年内就改变了我们对物理学、力和引力的理解。

gravity.en: Planets are much bigger, therefore have a larger gravitational pull, and are circular in shape, because of gravity.
gravity.zh: 行星要大得多，因此具有更强的引力，而且在引力的作用下呈圆形。

gravity.en: But it's not gravity. It's not inevitable.
gravity.zh: 但这不是万有引力那样的定律。它并非注定如此。

grief.en: In his grief, the king jumped off a cliff into the sea.
grief.zh: 在悲痛中，国王跳崖殉海。

grin.en: And I knew what I could do to say to this therapist, some, you know, to just sort of veer off a little and create some nice story, put a bow on it, push it across the table and watch your eyes light up a little bit, like a little grin or a self-deprecating joke or whatever.
grin.zh: 我知道我可以对这个治疗师说什么，你知道，稍微偏离一下，编造一些漂亮的故事，给它打个结，推到桌子对面，看着你的眼睛亮起来，比如一个小小的咧嘴笑或自嘲的笑话什么的。
